themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints spiked to 14 THIS WEEK compared to a 2.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 559% increase (z-score: 6.04)—suggesting either a sudden influx of unpermitted vendors or a coordinated enforcement crackdown on the Upper East Side.
evidence: 14 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (559% spike, z-score 6.04)
Spike is extremely recent and highly statistically anomalous
Vendor Enforcement ranks 6th in overall 90-day complaint volume (409 total), indicating existing neighborhood friction
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department or Dept. of Health about sudden vendor enforcement action on UES this week
Canvass Madison Ave and Lexington Ave to identify which vendor types are triggering complaints (food trucks, carts, pop-ups)

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints originating from parks jumped to 3 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 0.1 weekly complaints—a 2,300% spike (z-score: 8.69, highest statistical severity on the list)—indicating a significant and sudden disturbance.
evidence: 3 park noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2,300% increase, z-score 8.69—highest statistical anomaly)
Noise-related complaints dominate overall 311 volume (Noise-Residential: 841, Noise-Commercial: 356, Noise: 736 over 90 days)
Secondary spike in Noise - Street/Sidewalk (45 complaints last week vs 20.9 avg, 116% increase) suggests broader noise escalation
reporting_angles: Identify which UES parks (Central Park edge, smaller neighborhood parks) are generating complaints and what activity triggered them (concerts, events, construction)
Interview Parks Department about any recent large events, renovations, or permit changes

themes_detail.label: Illegal Parking Spike Persists
themes_detail.summary: Illegal parking complaints reached 240 LAST WEEK versus a 128.5 weekly average—an 87% spike (z-score: 5.07)—maintaining elevated levels as a persistent operational headache for the neighborhood.
evidence: 240 illegal parking complaints LAST WEEK vs. 128.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (87% increase, z-score 5.07)
Illegal Parking is the #1 complaint type overall over 90 days (1,875 complaints), indicating chronic infrastructure strain
Spike is sustained at elevated levels, not a one-time anomaly
reporting_angles: Cross-reference with DOB permit data (1,989 filings in last 90 days, mostly alterations) to determine if construction activity is blocking parking and driving complaints
Interview NYPD and DOT about enforcement capacity and whether staffing shortages are contributing to the surge

themes_detail.label: Street/Sidewalk Noise Doubles
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints reached 45 LAST WEEK compared to a 20.9 weekly average—a 116% increase (z-score: 4.21)—suggesting escalating outdoor disturbances beyond parks.
evidence: 45 Street/Sidewalk noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 20.9 weekly average (116% increase, z-score 4.21)
Converges with park noise spike (3 complaints) and general Noise category dominance—noise is the 3rd/4th/5th ranking complaint type overall
Unleashed dogs also spiked (4 complaints vs 0.4 avg, 967% increase), potentially contributing to outdoor disturbances
reporting_angles: Determine if street noise spike correlates with construction activity (1,989 DOB filings) or seasonal nightlife/outdoor dining expansion
Investigate whether the recent unleashed dog spike and street noise spike are connected (dogs in parks, on streets)

themes_detail.label: Unleashed Dogs and Dumpster Issues
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints spiked to 4 LAST WEEK from a 0.4 weekly baseline—a 967% increase (z-score: 7.49)—while dumpster complaints also hit 4 from 0.5 average, both representing acute but narrow emerging problems.
evidence: 4 unleashed dog complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (967% spike, z-score 7.49)
4 dumpster complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 7.0)
Both are ultra-low baseline issues that spiked suddenly, suggesting possible localized incident cluster rather than systemic problem
reporting_angles: Canvass Central Park edges and dog parks to determine if complaints are concentrated in one location or neighborhood-wide
Determine if dumpster complaints relate to construction activity or inadequate waste management infrastructure
